name: Sliding genioplasty

lead: Sliding genioplasty reshapes the chin by moving the bone itself. The surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and slides it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, which changes chin projection and width for a stronger, more balanced profile.

Unlike an implant, it uses your own bone, fixed in the new position with plates and screws. It is used for cosmetic chin reshaping, facial feminization and as part of face-contouring and jaw surgery. Evidence consists mostly of case series and reviews, with few comparative trials.

paras: People usually have it done as a planned operation, sometimes alone and sometimes together with other jaw procedures. The result becomes visible as swelling settles. On forums it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option, often compared with chin implants.
Reported problems include swelling, temporary lip and chin numbness, infection, displacement of the bone segment and, more rarely, nerve damage. It does not correct the bite.

angle.text: A stronger, better-balanced chin and profile. The chin bone is cut and moved forward, back or sideways, changing projection or width in a way you can see once healing is done. Evidence is mostly case series with few comparative trials.

lead: Sliding genioplasty is a chin surgery in which a surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and moves it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, then fixes it in place [1][2]. Unlike an implant, it uses the patient's own bone.

It is used for cosmetic chin reshaping, in facial feminization, and as part of face-contouring and jaw surgery [3][4][5]. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option, often compared with chin implants [6].
infobox: Oral and maxillofacial or plastic surgeons
Titanium plate and screws, or wires

paras: Wikipedia describes cutting a horseshoe-shaped piece of the lower jaw border and repositioning it, held with a titanium step plate and screws; it may be combined with rhinoplasty [1]. A paper on feminization states sliding genioplasty has the most potential for dramatic reshaping while avoiding implant issues, and that the mental nerve can be protected during surgery [3].

Uses documented in the literature include facial feminization [3], contouring a square jaw in East Asian patients combined with mandibular surgery [4][7], and balancing facial aesthetics [8]. Genioplasty does not correct bite; a significant overbite may need orthognathic surgery [1].

Reported effects include swelling, hematoma, and temporary lip weakness or numbness; less common are infection, displacement and nerve damage [1]. A 1996 paper addressed avoiding mental nerve injuries [2].

A systematic review looked at soft-to-hard tissue ratios in chin procedures including sliding genioplasty [9]. A ten-year surgeon experience series described sliding osteotomy for aesthetic balance [8]. A registered trial compared fat or PEEK onlay augmentation with sliding genioplasty for deficient chin in 12 patients [10]. A study assessed YouTube videos on genioplasty as a source of information [11]. Wikipedia says its sources are mainly case series and reviews and lack comparative trial data [1].

Users on looksmax.org ask whether a genioplasty would widen or advance a chin, whether to choose it over an implant, and how to evaluate outcomes such as asymmetry after surgery [6][12][13]. One poster reported a surgeon advising typical advancements of 6 to 7 mm [12]. Surgeons quoted by posters have also said swelling can look asymmetric early on [13].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, sliding genioplasty is discussed as a way to improve profile or chin width, often weighed against implants or jaw surgery [6][12].
